headline: Three redundant C509 spellings are refused, so a certificate has one encoding and an issuer signature cannot cover two different C509 byte strings.
summary:
The C509 draft encodes a certificate serial number, an authorityKeyIdentifier serial, and an RSA modulus and exponent as unwrapped CBOR unsigned bignums, and section 3.1.2 requires that any leading 0x00 byte be omitted. The decoder refused a redundant leading zero only when the value was two octets or longer, so a zero serial had two accepted spellings, the empty byte string and a lone 0x00, and both reconstructed byte-identical DER. For a certificate whose signature is computed over that reconstruction, one issuer signature therefore validated two distinct C509 byte strings, which defeats identifying, deduplicating, caching or blocklisting a certificate by its encoded form. Any leading zero is now refused, leaving the empty byte string as the single encoding of zero, and the same rule covers all four fields.

pki.schema.c509.encode now refuses a serialNumberHex that is not an even-length hexadecimal string. It previously decoded as much as it could and discarded the rest, so an odd-length or partly non-hexadecimal value silently became a different, still-valid serial number that the encoder's own re-parse could not detect: a caller asking for 0f5 received a certificate carrying 0x0f.

Two further fields carried a second spelling of one value. An RSA subjectPublicKey whose exponent is 65537 is written as the bare modulus, and a notAfter of 99991231235959Z is written as the CBOR simple value null; both values were also accepted in their longer forms, and both reconstructed the same DER. Each longer form is now refused.

This release also pins the refusal paths of the C509 decoder that had no test driving them: the byte cap on an unsigned bignum, an algorithm identifier slot that is not an unwrapped OID byte string, and one refusal for each extension decoder, together with the result-shape contract the encoder holds a caller to and the fallback that carries an extension value the compact forms cannot represent.

Security: pki.schema.c509.parse refuses an unsigned bignum whose first octet is 0x00, including a value that is only that octet, so every number has exactly one C509 encoding (draft sec. 3.1.2). A zero serial previously had two spellings that reconstructed byte-identical DER, letting one issuer signature cover two distinct C509 certificates. The rule covers the certificate serial number, the authorityKeyIdentifier serial, and the RSA modulus and exponent.

pki.schema.c509.parse refuses an RSA subjectPublicKey written as [modulus, 65537] instead of the bare modulus. Draft sec. 3.1.9 omits the array and the exponent when the exponent is 65537, so the array spelling of such a key is a second encoding of one certificate, reconstructing byte-identical DER. An RSA key with any other exponent still uses the array form.

pki.schema.c509.parse refuses a notAfter written as the epoch 253402300799 rather than the CBOR simple value null. Draft sec. 3.1.5 encodes the no-expiration time 99991231235959Z as null, so the explicit epoch is a second spelling that reconstructs the same GeneralizedTime and therefore the same DER. A notBefore is unaffected, and pki.schema.c509.encode refuses that Date on notAfter instead of emitting a form the decoder rejects.
Fixed: pki.schema.c509.encode refuses a serialNumberHex that is not an even-length hexadecimal string instead of decoding a prefix of it. An odd-length or partly non-hexadecimal value previously became a different, valid serial number without any error, which the encoder's own re-parse could not catch. The check applies whether the result is re-emitted from its preserved field bytes or built field by field, so a caller is told the value is malformed rather than having it quietly ignored.
